relevance_note: Multicenter Turkish LAD-I cohort with per-patient tables of demographics and ITGB2 mutations: 'Nine distinct variants in the ITGB2 gene in 13 of the 15 patients with LAD-I were characterized'.
method_note: The Markdown is the Research Square preprint (Posted Date: March 24th, 2021) of the article; the header says a version of record was published later, so values come from the preprint text. Tables 1 and 2 were transcribed by a short Python script that copies cells and row segments from the paper file; output was checked against both tables by eye. Labels: Table 1 marks P5, P6, P14 and P15 with '*' but no legend defines the asterisk, so it was not interpreted (labels recorded without it, as in Table 2 and P1-P15 otherwise). Ages: onset from Table 1 'Symptomatic Age (Days)' and diagnosis from 'Age at Diagnosis (Months)'; the unit comes from the column header. Consanguinity: '+' recorded as yes; P13 '-' recorded as no, supported by the text count 'Fourteen (93%) patients had consanguineous parents' (14 '+' cells). P1 is compound heterozygous; cDNA and protein were paired in printed order ('c.533C>T and c.1777C>T' / 'Pro178Leu and Arg593Cys'). Transcript NM_000211.5 is taken from the Figure 3 legend, which says mutation positions were drawn on that reference sequence. P14 and P15 have 'n/a' in Table 2 and get no variant rows; the text says 'two patients had died before analysis' without naming them, so vital status is 'not reported' for everyone. Deaths (2 from infection, 2 after HSCT), HSCT in 4 patients, and all clinical features (delayed cord separation 12/15, omphalitis 8/15, leukocytosis 14/15, diarrhea 6, fungal infections 3, etc.) are reported only as counts or for unidentified patients ('a 21-year-old male patient' with periodontal destruction, 'a 4-year-old male patient' with gingivitis, 'a patient with alopecia areata'); none can be tied to a table label, so no extra rows were created and all checklist items are 'not reported'. 'We did not observe autoimmune findings in our cohort except in a patient with alopecia areata' excludes no specific person because the exception is unidentified. The Discussion describes a c.305_306delAA homozygote whose CD18 was absent with one antibody clone but higher with another (CD11a/b/c 0%, 1%, 7%); only P12 among the four c.305_306delAA carriers has 0% in Table 2, but the paper does not name the patient, so this was not assigned. CD18 expression from Table 2 is recorded as a per-person laboratory finding and as functional evidence. No contradictions found; Table 2 counts (9 distinct variants, 13 genotyped; 11 with CD18 <2%, 4 with 2-8%) agree with the text.
